stories.headline: High-speed train crash in Spain kills at least 68
body: At least 68 people died when a high-speed train from Madrid slammed into the back of another near Urda, in Toledo province.
Officials suggested an 'inexplicable' error at the central control centre; dozens more were injured.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning. It is Spain's second deadly high-speed crash this year.
stories.vc: Two fatal crashes in a year will push Spain to spend on rail signalling and safety systems, a niche where rail-tech suppliers compete.

stories.headline: Israel's count shows Netanyahu leading, but no majority
body: With most votes counted, Netanyahu's Likud leads Gadi Eisenkot's party, but no side has a clear path to a majority.
Opposition parties together, including two Arab-led factions, won more votes than Netanyahu's right-wing bloc.
Both leaders claimed success overnight; coalition talks will decide who governs.
stories.joke: Both sides say they won. The 61-seat maths says: not yet.
stories.vc: Political limbo delays big budget and defence decisions that Israel's tech sector watches closely.

stories.statLabel: Iraqi PM visit since Assad fell
stories.headline: Iraq's prime minister makes a historic visit to Syria
body: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus, the first such visit since Bashar al-Assad fell.
They discussed sending Iraqi oil through Syria's Baniyas pipeline, more trade and farming projects.
Iraq began exporting small amounts of oil via Syria after the US-led war on Iran disrupted routes.
stories.joke: Old neighbours, new pipeline, same complicated group chat.
stories.vc: A working Iraq–Syria oil route would add supply outside the Strait of Hormuz, good for oil importers like India.

stories.statLabel: above IPO price on day one
stories.headline: Jio Platforms jumps 27% on its stock market debut
body: Jio Platforms closed its first trading day at ₹1,417.35, up 26.66% from its IPO price of ₹1,119.
That makes it India's second-most valuable listed company, worth about ₹13.05 lakh crore, behind parent Reliance.
The ₹30,213 crore IPO, India's largest, was subscribed 22 times; most of the money will repay debt.
stories.joke: Most of us can't get a Jio refund. Investors got 27% on day one.
stories.vc: A blockbuster listing revives India's IPO pipeline and gives later tech listings a strong benchmark.

stories.headline: Cognizant may invest in Sarvam at up to $4 billion valuation
body: IT giant Cognizant is reportedly in talks to invest in Bengaluru AI startup Sarvam as part of a $300 million raise.
The deal could value Sarvam at $3.5–4 billion, more than double its $1.5 billion valuation in June.
HCLTech already put $150 million into Sarvam; Cognizant would be the second IT services major on board.
stories.joke: Indian IT's new strategy: if you can't build the AI, buy a slice of it.
stories.vc: Strategic money from IT firms gives Indian AI labs both cash and a built-in sales channel to enterprise clients.

stories.headline: Namma Metro's Pink Line may open on 15 November
body: The 7.5-km elevated stretch of the Pink Line between Kalena Agrahara and Tavarekere got its safety clearance on Wednesday.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar hinted PM Modi may inaugurate it on 15 November.
Minister Krishna Byre Gowda says the date is not yet confirmed.
stories.joke: Bengaluru metro: arriving soon™ since forever. This time with a safety certificate.
stories.vc: Each new metro line lifts property and retail demand around its stations, a big theme for Bengaluru real estate.

stories.statLabel: Microsoft revenue from OpenAI in a quarter
stories.headline: Microsoft made $10 billion from OpenAI in one quarter
body: Microsoft earned $10 billion from deals with OpenAI in July–September, nearly 11% of its $92.3 billion revenue.
At that pace it would make about $40 billion a year from OpenAI.
OpenAI also owed Microsoft $7.2 billion at the end of September, up from $6 billion in June.
stories.joke: Partners, rivals and now 11% of the bill. Complicated.
stories.vc: Shows how much of Big Tech's AI revenue rests on a few labs; if OpenAI slows, Microsoft feels it.

stories.headline: Microsoft reveals Azure's revenue for the first time: $33.2B
body: Microsoft disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars for the first time: $33.2 billion, up 48%.
Google Cloud made $30.7 billion in the same quarter, but grew about twice as fast.
It was Microsoft's 10th record quarter in a row.
stories.joke: After years of 'trust us, it's growing', Microsoft finally showed the receipt.
stories.vc: Clear numbers make cloud stocks easier to compare, and show AI demand is still pushing cloud spending up fast.

stories.headline: Alphabet stock falls 8% as search ad growth slows
body: Alphabet's revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, but search revenue grew only 12%, down from 19% in the first quarter.
Shares fell 8% after the results.
Google is now rolling out ads inside its AI search answers in more countries.
stories.joke: When your AI answers the question, nobody clicks the ad. Awkward.
stories.vc: If AI answers eat search ads, the whole web's ad economy shifts; startups that sell AI ad tools stand to gain.

stories.headline: The US Fed keeps interest rates on hold
body: The Federal Reserve held its key rate at 3.75–4% in a 10–2 vote, its last decision before the US midterms.
It said the economy is growing strongly and spending has held up, despite rising inflation.
Markets had priced in a more than 90% chance of no change.
stories.joke: The Fed's big announcement: nothing. Markets: 'Thank you.'
stories.vc: Higher-for-longer US rates keep the dollar strong and make funding costlier for emerging-market startups.

stories.headline: Kodiak lands its first big deal for driverless highway trucks
body: Self-driving truck firm Kodiak AI will deliver 75 driverless trucks to freight company DTL Transport from 2028.
It is Kodiak's first binding deal for big rigs on public highways.
In December it plans to start hauling Ikea goods between Dallas and Houston with no safety driver.
stories.joke: The truck will drive itself. The playlist is still up to you.
stories.vc: Binding orders, not pilots, are what investors need to believe autonomous trucking makes money.
